title: Atonement
definition: The atonement is the saving work of Jesus Christ by which He offered Himself for sinners, bearing sin and reconciling believers to God.
summary: Through His death, Jesus paid for sin and reconciled sinners to God.
christFocus: Christ is the spotless substitute who died for sinners, satisfied divine justice, displayed divine love, and opened the way to reconciliation with God.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The atonement stands at the heart of the Gospel. Sin separates humanity from the holy God, and sinners cannot remove their guilt by effort, emotion, religion, or good intentions. God Himself provides the sacrifice in Christ.

Jesus willingly gave Himself for sinners. He bore sin, endured judgment, fulfilled righteousness, and reconciled His people to God. The cross displays both the seriousness of sin and the depth of God's love.

Because of the atonement, forgiveness is not pretend mercy. God does not ignore sin; He deals with it through the sacrifice of His Son. Those who trust in Christ are cleansed, forgiven, and brought near.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Many people carry guilt, shame, fear, and the burden of trying to make themselves acceptable to God. The atonement matters because it shows that salvation rests on Christ's finished work, not human performance.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Bring guilt to the cross instead of hiding it or trying to pay for it yourself. Trust Christ's finished work, confess sin honestly, forgive others from the grace you have received, and live in grateful obedience.
